corpus: public GitHub repositories' .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json files, taken from GitHub code search (query: "hooks" "command" path:.claude filename:settings.json), first 500 results, 355 unique, fetched at the indexed commit from raw.githubusercontent.com; search-ranked, not star-ranked, and not committed to this repository
matcher_misfires_found_and_fixed: case-pattern word `*rg\ *)` taken as a command (glob characters now rejected)
`2>/dev/null` after a subshell taken as a command (redirections now rejected)
reading: Every remaining match that was read is a script the repository ships (a formatter, guard, notifier or session helper, commonly under .claude/hooks/ or $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR); none of the 285 files is known to be malicious. HOOK-003 cannot tell a team's own hook script from a planted loader, so this is the share of ordinary hook-using repositories it reports, not a measured false-positive rate against attacks.
reproduce: Fetch the files, place each at <dir>/.claude/settings.json and run ConfigHygieneAnalyzer().analyze_config on it; count HOOK-003.
severity_reason: 65% of hook-bearing files fire and none is known malicious; precision against planted loaders in this sample is about zero.
